info.title: Example Internal API
info.description:
# Introduction

Every request is authenticated with a bearer token.

parameters.name: filters
parameters.description: Filters: a JSON object, URL-encoded under the one key, e.g. filters={"status":{"$eq":"active"}}. The entries of a document AND together. A field takes a value, matched for equality, or an object of operators. $and and $or take a non-empty list of filter documents, joined by AND or OR, e.g. filters={"status":"active","$or":[{"role":"admin"},{"role":"owner"}]}. A traversable relation key takes a filter document for the related resource. $has and $hasnt take a relation name, a list of names, or relation names keyed to filter documents. $scope invokes the named scopes the resource declares: a scope name, a list of names, or names keyed to objects of arguments, e.g. filters={"$scope":{"near":{"lat":51.5,"lng":-0.12,"km":5}}}. The schema lists the fields, operators and values this resource accepts; a date-time is sent in the form the field emits. A document is held to at most 8192 bytes encoded, 16 levels of JSON nesting, 3 levels of groups and relations, 100 keys in all.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Ordering: a comma-separated list of keys, each optionally suffixed with :asc or :desc in any case, e.g. order=name,created_at:desc. Any other direction, or a repeated key, is rejected. The key is appended last when the order lacks it, so tied rows never repeat or go missing between pages. Random order and columns that admit null cannot order a cursor-paginated read. order=relevance ranks rows by how closely they match search: the whole value, then the start, then the start of a word, then anywhere; it needs search and offset pagination. A sortable aggregate orders by aggregates.<key>, e.g. order=aggregates.posts_count:desc, and a sortable to-one relation by a sortable column of the resource it renders, e.g. order=customer.name; neither can order a cursor-paginated read, and a NULL value sorts where the database places NULL.

200.description: A paginated collection of resources. Length-aware by default; sending ?cursor or ?pagination=cursor returns the cursor shape.

total.description: The records the query matches, or only those offset pagination can reach when the total is capped.

total_capped.description: Whether more records match than the total reports; read past it with cursor pagination.

Fields.name: fields
Fields.description: Sparse fieldsets keyed by resource _type, e.g. fields[users]=id,name. Each value is a comma-separated list of that schema's property names, with aggregates selecting its aggregates payload, or :all to select every field. Unknown types and names are rejected. A type with no key selects its schema's x-default-fields, unless a parent relation pins its fields. A selected property may still be left out; only the required ones are always returned.

Search.name: search
Search.description: Free-text search across the fields a resource declares searchable, e.g. search=John Smith. It matches the requested resource only and never traverses a relation; a term carrying a word shorter than the configured minimum is rejected, as is one longer, or carrying more words, than the configured bounds allow. The length is counted once surrounding and repeated whitespace has been collapsed, so a term written with more characters than the maximum may still be accepted.

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: Page size: the maximum number of records to return per page. A request above the ceiling is rejected rather than reduced to it.

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description: Opaque cursor token for cursor pagination. A token that does not decode, or does not match the requested order, is rejected; restart from the first page.

Pagination.name: pagination
Pagination.description: Pagination mode: set to cursor to switch from the default length-aware pagination to cursor pagination. Any other non-empty value is rejected.

Aggregates.name: aggregates
Aggregates.description: Relation aggregates: request the keys of the resource's aggregates object per resource type, e.g. aggregates[users]=posts_count. Requesting any aggregate replaces the defaults of that type. A type's aggregates apply wherever it renders, at the root or embedded, when its fields select aggregates, except under a relation whose resource type varies per record. Unknown resource types and names are rejected.

Trashed.name: trashed
Trashed.description: Soft-delete visibility: with returns soft-deleted records alongside the live ones and only returns the soft-deleted records alone, e.g. trashed=with. Omitting it returns live records only. An included relation follows it where its resource opts in and otherwise stays live. A resource that has not opted in to exposing its soft-deleted records, or a caller it does not permit, gets a 422.

Total-Count.description: The total number of records across all pages of the length-aware collection, absent when the total is capped.

ETag.description: The weak entity tag of the stored resource, to send in If-Match on a write that must not overwrite a newer state.
